title: Experts disagree on .paqad/ledger/authoring/delegations.jsonl
context:
Chief architect: This holds a must-level security-auditor constraint, so the owner rules it. The other two claims do not contradict it and the plan should keep them: one row per delegation keyed on the Agent tool call's tool_use_id (also accepted as EX-user-flow-writer-7), and a catalog report that says the 30-day never-fired count covers this machine only. That matches the #794 activation log, which is local operational data.

Target: .paqad/ledger/authoring/delegations.jsonl
- security-auditor: The delegation log records only {agent, request_id, session_id, at, tokens, duration_ms, status}; it never stores the delegation message, the report text or tool output, which can carry secrets or personal data.
- devops-engineer: the ledger/ ignore rule (gitignore-writer.ts:62) keeps the delegation log and high-table-benchmark.json per machine, so the 30-day retirement check (AC-P06) and the benchmark numbers only reflect one machine; the spec must say so or move the benchmark result into tracked evidence
- integration-architect: one delegation fires both the new PostToolUse Agent|Task entry and the new SubagentStop entry, and a background agent's PostToolUse fires at launch before tokens and duration are final; each row must carry the tool_use_id from the Agent tool call as request_id, and the catalog and learn readers must merge rows by that key so one delegation is counted once, whatever order the two events arrive in
